flawed_step: The claim ignores that equal-weight ties can produce different minimum spanning trees.
counterexample: Let the graph be a triangle on vertices A, B, C, with all three edges AB, AC, BC having weight 1. A legal Kruskal run orders tied edges AB, then BC, then AC, producing {AB, BC}. A legal Prim run starts at A, chooses AC over the tied edge AB, then chooses BC over AB, producing {AC, BC}. The edge sets differ, and both are spanning trees of total weight 2, hence both are minimum spanning trees.
assessment_summary: A connected weighted graph can have multiple minimum spanning trees. Unspecified tie-breaking allows Kruskal and Prim to return different ones.
